- Which Redwood legal entity should issue the credit/offset if we net?

Hi Susan — thanks for the note and the context. Short answers up front: we can support netting/crediting across invoices, but the VAT treatment depends on which Lumina legal entity is contracted on each invoice and whether you can provide a validated VAT registration (VIES check) for the EU entity.

To give you a recommended path:
1) If both invoices are B2B and Lumina can provide valid VAT IDs for each billed entity, we will apply reverse-charge on the EU-supplied line items and issue a credit note from the Redwood legal entity that issued the original invoice.
2) If you want a single payment routed to Redwood EU (to simplify reconciliation), we can issue a credit to offset the UK-billed invoice and re-issue a single consolidated invoice to the Lumina EU entity — but we will need your confirmation that Lumina has the authority to net inter-company obligations.

Please confirm the exact Lumina legal names and VAT IDs for both invoices (copy/paste is fine). Once we have the VAT IDs we run an internal VIES lookup and, if needed, vault the VAT certificate. Vanessa (cc) will handle the credit-note flow and timing.

Next steps I propose:
- You send VAT IDs and any VAT certificate PDFs (attach).
- Vanessa will confirm credit note timeline (typically 3–5 business days for processing and reissue).
- We’ll confirm the collection path and whether any bank routing or withholding changes are needed.

If you prefer a quick call to run through the steps, happy to set 20 minutes.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Hi Susan — looping in Finance Ops (Lauren) to confirm the internal steps. Thanks Marcus for the rundown. A few process details from our side: 

- VAT validation: we require either a VIES-validated VAT ID or a national VAT registration certificate. A PDF of the VAT certificate is acceptable for our records; please include the registration number, legal name, and effective date.

- Credit / netting approach options (pick one):
  * Credit note + consolidated invoice: Redwood issues a credit note against one invoice and re-issues a consolidated invoice to the designated Lumina legal entity. This preserves audit trail and ensures VAT is charged/zero-rated appropriately. Estimated processing: 3 business days after VAT validation.
  * Inter-company netting (Lumina instructs): Lumina provides written authorization that two billed entities may net obligations and confirms which entity will be the payer. We will accept a single payment only after receiving that authorization and a VAT certificate for the paying entity. Processing: up to 5 business days to update accounting entries.

- Withholding: as long as Lumina is purchasing as a B2B and reverse-charge is applied (valid VAT ID on file), there should be no additional withholding from Redwood’s perspective. If Lumina instructs payment from a non-EU bank or a different treasury entity, we’ll confirm the bank routing but typically that does not change VAT treatment.

Attached is a draft credit-note template we use (proposed-credit-note-REDWOOD-INV-5043.pdf). If you choose the consolidated invoice route, we’ll prepare the credit and send the new invoice to the Lumina EU entity you designate.

Please attach the VAT certificate PDF and confirm which route you want to take.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
